stem:
A steel sphere of mass 0.29 kg is suspended in equilibrium from a vertical spring. The centre of the sphere is 8.5 cm from the top of the spring, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The sphere is now set in motion so that it is moving in a horizontal circle at constant speed, as shown in Fig. 2.2.

[[fig:f2]]

The distance from the centre of the sphere to the top of the spring is now 10.8 cm.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, with reference to the forces acting on the sphere, why the length of the spring in Fig. 2.2 is greater than in Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: The angle between the linear axis of the spring and the vertical is 27°.
parts.text: Show that the radius *r* of the circle is 4.9 cm.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the tension in the spring is 3.2 N.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The spring obeys Hooke’s law.

Calculate the spring constant, in N cm⁻¹, of the spring.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Use the information in (b) to determine the centripetal acceleration of the sphere.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the period of the circular motion of the sphere.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: A steel sphere hangs from a vertical spring attached to a horizontal support, with a vertical distance of 8.5 cm marked from the support to the sphere’s centre.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.2
figures.alt: A sphere moves in a horizontal circle at the end of a slanted spring, with the radius, a 27° angle to the vertical, and a spring length of 10.8 cm indicated.
